operations.evidence: Where nationality was known, 1,870 of 1,949 linked arrests, or 96%, were self-defined British or British dual nationality.
Self-defined nationality does not indicate origin, conduct or parcel risk.
The release notes that nationality is declared at arrest and may differ from country of origin.
Nationality categories must not be treated as ethnicity, residence or location risk.
The 242 non-linked arrests represented a 2% increase from 238 in the previous year.
A small national change is not evidence of a local trend.
Of the 242 non-linked arrests, 67 were charged.
Charge counts are provisional case outcomes and not parcel indicators.
Of the 242 non-linked arrests, 52 were released without charge.
Release without charge illustrates why arrests must not be equated with guilt.
Six of the 242 non-linked arrests had alternative action.
Alternative action combines several possible resolutions and cannot support local scoring.
Seven of the 242 non-linked arrests had a decision pending.
Pending cases are incomplete and should not be treated as final outcomes.
One hundred and ten of the 242 non-linked arrests were bailed to return or released under investigation.
These cases were unresolved at the data cutoff.
Of the 67 charged individuals, 52 were charged under terrorism-related legislation.
Charge classification does not establish conviction or parcel risk.
Twelve individuals were charged under section 5 of the Terrorism Act 2006 for preparation of terrorist acts.
The count is national and cannot be attributed to a neighbourhood.
Eleven individuals were charged under section 58 of the Terrorism Act 2000 for collection of information useful to terrorism.
Charges are allegations and not parcel-level evidence.
Nine individuals charged with terrorism-related offences were prosecuted and all nine were convicted.
This subset is based on progressed cases and is not representative of all arrests.
Forty of the 3,061 arrests, or 1%, were made under section 41 of the Terrorism Act 2000.
The statistic describes arresting legislation, not local incidence.
The remaining 3,021 arrests, or 99%, were made under other legislation, including PACE.
The category includes non-terrorism legislation and requires careful interpretation.
From January to March 2026, there were 14 instances where a request for access to a solicitor was delayed.
This procedural count is not a parcel-level safety measure.
Of 551 total charges, 536 were for terrorism-related offences.
The classification can include charges under non-terrorism legislation considered terrorism-related.
Among 3,055 arrests where sex was known, 1,467 were female and 1,587 male.
Recorded-sex aggregates must not be used for individual or location profiling.
Among 241 non-linked arrests where sex was known, 219 were male and 22 female.
Demographic composition is descriptive and not a local risk indicator.
Persons aged 30 and above accounted for 2,671 arrests, or 87%, where age was known.
Age-group proportions cannot support parcel-level inference.
Court proceedings data are based on trial completion date and are not directly comparable with arrest-outcome data based on arrest date.
Different time bases must not be combined as if they were one cohort.
